stop_condition: The disk-derived governing-round comparison is retired with no surviving second opinion about what governs; Shape A promotion still works; the R15-F3 fields reach a mechanical reader additively; and the full L1 tier holds its completeness floor with no new failure.

findings.evidence: qa-gate.sh runs under `set -e` (line 196). The new gate consultation `unrecorded_gate_out=$(CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$PROJECT_DIR" bash "$REVIEW_CHECK_SCRIPT" gate "$tid" 2>/dev/null)` is a BARE assignment from a command substitution, and it is the only unguarded one of the four `review-check.sh gate` call sites in this file (4705 uses `|| review_rc=$?`; 5839 and 8762 use `|| true`). `gate` exits 4 on every refusal, so the assignment aborts cmd_approve on the spot. STRUCTURAL PROOF that this kills exactly the two branches the fix's safety argument rests on: review-check.sh has exactly ONE `emit_gate 0` (line 3462), reached only after ART_ITER is extracted at 3118 from a grammar-validated `^REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 iteration=[0-9]+` prefix, so gate exit 0 always implies a numeric `.artifact.iteration` and therefore branch 1. Branches 2 (`elif [ "$unrecorded_gate_ekey" = "review_artifact_missing" ]`, 5117) and 3 (the `else` at 5128, the fix's headline 'this refusal will NOT guess which listed file should be recorded') both require a non-numeric iteration, hence a non-zero gate exit, hence the abort one line earlier. MEASURED A/B in an isolated fixture (own bd store, own CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR): shipped script, F1-shaped task (--no-review, zero REVIEW-ARTIFACT records, one stray unrecorded artifact under docs/reviews/) -> approve rc=4 with ZERO bytes on stdout AND stderr, no error_key, no observations, no remediation. Add the same single `|| true` the sibling sites use (one changed line, `bash -n` clean) and the SAME task -> rc=4, 1884 bytes, error_key=review_artifact_unrecorded (the key docs document), observations 'no governing record exists yet' naming the r1 file to record. Second A/B on the else branch: shipped -> 0 bytes, 'will NOT guess' absent; guarded -> 1676 bytes, 'will NOT guess' present, and NO --file named (the intended behaviour). REACHABLE FROM THE SHIPPED STOP HOOK: verify-before-stop.sh:4539-4541 calls `approve --no-review`, and the bullet added THIS round at 4587-4598 documents `review_artifact_unrecorded` as reachable there for exactly this stray-artifact shape - a key the code cannot emit in the typical F1 sub-case. REGRESSION OF A NAMED, ALREADY-FIXED SHAPE: ERREXIT-HASH-GUARD (claude-workflow-plugin-qzv.3) at qa-gate.sh:4439 and 4505 fixed this identical mechanism in this identical function, and its comment reads verbatim '`|| current_hash=""` is not defensive noise: without it this refusal is DEAD CODE.' verify-before-stop.sh:4650-4657 still asserts that fix holds. WHY THE SUITE IS GREEN OVER IT: every 8.7 leg (A/B/C) and the 8.7.E META strip use scenarios where gate exits 0, so branches 2 and 3 have no leg at all - neither positive nor negative - which is the CLAUDE.md pairing requirement unmet for the two new branches.
findings.description: The R15-F1 fix consults review-check.sh gate through an unguarded command substitution under set -e, so both of its non-happy-path branches are provably dead code and approve dies with a bare exit 4 and no envelope on a Stop-hook-reachable path. The round's headline safety claim - 'when gate cannot establish a governing record for any reason other than none-exist-yet, the refusal names no file at all' - never executes. Mitigated (not CRITICAL) because verify-before-stop.sh fails closed on an unparseable envelope, so nothing releases. Fix: `|| true` (or `|| unrecorded_gate_rc=$?`) on line 5085, matching 5839/8762, plus a test leg driving gate to a non-zero exit with an unrecorded artifact present - the P15 and P17 shapes above are ready-made.

findings.evidence: The enumeration glob `for unrecorded_f in "$PROJECT_DIR/$REVIEW_ARTIFACT_SUBDIR/$unrecorded_sanitized_tid"-r*.json` has no readability precondition on the directory, and an unlistable directory is indistinguishable from an empty one to a glob, so the `if [ "${#unrecorded_disk_artifacts[@]}" -eq 0 ]` arm at 4962 reports the affirmative PASS 'no on-disk review artifact for <tid> under docs/reviews/ (nothing to reconcile)'. MEASURED A/B on ONE task, same records, same files on disk, only variable the permission bit: docs/reviews at 0755 -> approve rc=4, error_key=review_artifact_unrecorded (correct); docs/reviews at 0000 -> approve rc=0, status=approved, labels=[qa-approved] - the gate RELEASED - while the unrecorded artifact was still present and still unrecorded (re-hashed independently: aaca4b31..., `recorded-hashes` index() -> false). Also reproduces at 0111 (traversable but not listable) -> rc=0. The healthy 'nothing unrecorded' control also returns rc=0, so the fail-open outcome is indistinguishable from a genuine pass. `[ -r ]` distinguishes cleanly (measured: -d yes, -r no, -x no at 0000). THIS REGION IS NEW IN THIS CHANGE SET, not pre-existing: `git diff -U0` shows `+ local -a unrecorded_disk_artifacts=()`, `+ ... -r*.json; do`, and `+ ... (nothing to reconcile)` as added lines. INCONSISTENT WITH ITS OWN BLOCK: the two sibling unavailability modes a few lines up both fail CLOSED by explicit design - review_check_unavailable ('This FAILS CLOSED by design (a deleted checker must not read as a passing check)', 4941) and review_recorded_hashes_unavailable ('This FAILS CLOSED', 4969) - so the third unavailability mode, the directory being enumerated, is the one that reads as a pass. REMEDY VERIFIED: a 7-line fail-closed precondition (`[ -d "$dir" ] && { [ ! -r "$dir" ] || [ ! -x "$dir" ]; }` -> emit_error_json review_dir_unreadable, exit 4) inserted before the glob gives rc=4/review_dir_unreadable on the 0000 case, and ALL THREE discriminators still pass: readable+unrecorded -> 4/review_artifact_unrecorded, readable+clean -> 0/approved, and directory ABSENT -> 0/approved (absent is legitimately not unreadable).
findings.description: An unreadable docs/reviews/ makes an unrecorded review artifact invisible to approve, which then sets qa-approved - reinstating this task's own headline defect ('the gate verifies a stale review') behind a single chmod, in code added by this change set, in a block whose two sibling unavailability modes both fail closed on purpose. The R15-F1 triggers the operator directed me to re-run were both permission-based on a FILE; this is the same operation one directory up.

findings.evidence: `unrecorded_this_iter=$(basename "$unrecorded_f" | sed -E "s/^${unrecorded_sanitized_tid}-r([0-9]+)\.json\$/\1/")` reads the iteration from the FILENAME, while review-record derives the canonical path from the artifact's own `.iterations` field (review_artifact_path_for, 6859). MEASURED with a file named -r99.json whose content says iterations=1: gate governs iteration=5, the advice takes the 'is a NEWER round' branch and names `review-record --file <...-r99.json>`, and following it fails with artifact_path_not_derived (rc=1). `review-reconcile` on the same file ALSO fails with artifact_path_not_derived, so neither remedy the refusal names can succeed and the only exit is the audited --accept-unrecorded-review, which the refusal does mention. Does NOT wedge anything: gate stays at iteration=5 with an empty error_key, and approve stays at rc=4. Reachability is low - both canonical writers derive the path from content, and codex-review.sh forces `.iterations=$ITER` (539) and `-r$ITER.json` (578) from the same variable, so only a hand-placed file produces the mismatch.
findings.description: On a filename-vs-content iteration mismatch the printed advice names two commands that both refuse, so the refusal is unfollowable as printed. Safe (no wedge, no fail-open) and hard to reach, but the message should either read the iteration from the artifact content or say that an unparseable/mismatched artifact must be removed or bypassed.

findings.evidence: The comparison is `[ -z "$unrecorded_max_iter" ] || [ "$unrecorded_gate_iter" -gt "$unrecorded_max_iter" ]`, so the EQUAL case falls to the else arm and prints 'is a NEWER round than that' about an iteration equal to the governing one. MEASURED via the content-drift trigger: record r5 through the real writer, then overwrite that same file with different bytes at the same iteration -> advice says the r5 file '(iteration=5)... is a NEWER round than' iteration=5. Following it is BENIGN: a second REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 record at iteration=5 lands, gate still resolves iteration=5 with an empty error_key, approve reaches rc=0. It also cannot launder an open finding - measured separately with an at-threshold critical on the recorded r5 and the file drifted to findings=[]: cmd_approve refuses with unresolved_findings BEFORE the unrecorded block, both before and after the drift, so the 'record this file' advice is never printed in that shape.
findings.description: Cosmetic mis-statement in the advice for the equal-iteration case ('NEWER' when it is equal), with a benign outcome and no security consequence. Worth a `-ge` or a third message arm.

findings.evidence: Read as the intended reader, the retained claim reads as a refuted dead claim, not a live assertion, on three structural signals: the introducer names it superseded BEFORE the quote ('THE CLAIM THIS REPLACES, held as fact here for two rounds:'), the claim is fenced in quotation marks, and the sentence immediately after the closing quote is the flat refutation 'It was not more robust.' The enclosing block header also states 'THE FIX IS NOT A FOURTH PATCH TO THIS COMPARISON-S DISK-DERIVED INPUT: it is retiring the DISK as a source for it.' The only residual is a grep hazard - a future `grep 'more robust'` surfaces the dead claim - which is not a reading hazard.
findings.description: Answering the orchestrator's explicit question: keeping the claim as an explicitly quoted and refuted dead claim is the stronger choice, and I agree with that call. Deleting it would have removed the only in-tree record of what was assumed and why it was wrong, which is the thing that stops a fifth attempt. No action.

findings.evidence: My prior R15-F4 is materially addressed: the '12 artifacts on disk against 3 recorded rounds' figure now carries 'at the time of that measurement', a note that i8cx's backlog has since been reconciled and no longer reproduces the shape, and a citation to where the number lives (review-check.sh's recorded-hashes header). It still does not carry the command that produced it and the commit it was measured at, which is what CONTRIBUTING.md:499-504 asks for.
